correctness.rationale: Covariance identity follows from exact joint pollinator-failure events and preserves all marginal terms under checkerboard swaps. All 36 guild-size pairs of positive integers with total at most nine were exhaustively generated. Each connected-incidence count matches an independently derived recurrence; each connected-output switch has integer transformed difference coefficients of one sign, certifying fixed sign over the entire continuum q in (0,1). The ten-species pair is directly connected, degree-preserving, has every vertex degree at least two, and its exact variance difference is independently recomputed by full failure-subset enumeration. Proof and complete C++17 verifier are included; finite experiments are not invoked as an infinite-order theorem.

value.rationale: Local degree-preserving rewiring is a common null-model or network-intervention operation. The total expected number of plant extinctions is unchanged because every plant degree is fixed; yet the variance ranking reverses as extinction severity crosses one half. This precisely isolates a risk-tail/uncertainty tradeoff invisible to degree-based expected losses. The sharp ten-species threshold and minimum-degree-two witness distinguish it from both arbitrary network rewiring and marginal-risk examples; it is a meaningful structural boundary and reproducible benchmark, not a routine parameter increment. Scope remains restricted to static homogeneous independent failure.
